- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk; add 2–4% downward buffer to forecast mean.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model fails to adjust; apply mean reversion rule: average last 5 days’ price + 10% of sentiment deviation.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count (≥18 events), model tends to overfit recent volatility; cap forecast range within ±15% of 14-day moving average.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model misreads trend; use weighted average of sentiment + 3-day moving average to smooth forecast.
